column1: # How long each bats test file took, in whole seconds of wall time. just test reads this record to
# split the test files into parts that take about as long, and fails while a test file has no line
# here, a line names a file tests/ no longer has, a second line names a file, or a line is not a
# test file, a tab and its whole seconds. scripts/test-run prints a file's time once its bats run
# ends, the run's start and the file's setup_file included, in a line of its own,
# test: tests/<name>.bats took <N>s, and scripts/test-times writes this record from those lines,
# through just test-time FILE... for the files run here and just test-times-record [RUN] for every
# file a CI run timed: a timed file gets its new time, a file not timed keeps its line, and a line
# just test refuses is dropped, with a line saying so.
# Columns, separated by a tab: the test file, the seconds it took.
